pass_b_english: …to our hearts, toward the illumination of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.

The mystagogue clarifies through the present word that faith is directed toward God, even if it were practiced in the face of Christ; for both Jews and Greeks have been called toward the experiential knowledge of Christ—the former as if from error and false worship toward the true knowledge of God, and the latter toward a more precise knowledge, being tutored by the Law.
Such is also the law-giving Paul, who is seen as having been slightly cautioned in comparison to those instructed in the lessons of the Law, because of the surpassing knowledge of Christ.

When, therefore, the mystagogues preach Christ, and those believing in God believe in the one and true God, how can Christ not be God? He is no bastard, no pseudonym, and certainly not a stranger to the Father, but rather truly is from Him according to His nature.
For the mind of those who wander has been reproached by an irrational and demonic deception, but God promised that the light would shine up upon us out of the darkness.
For he once said through the voice of Isaiah, "The people sitting in darkness, behold a great light; those dwelling in a land and shadow of death, light shall shine upon you" (Isaiah 9:2).

And the law-giving David says, speaking from the face of those in gloom and darkness, "That you light my lamp, Lord; you God, my God, you light my darkness" (Psalm 18:28). Since, therefore, the promise of the Father has been fulfilled for us, and the divine, intelligible light has dawned upon us, we have known His glory in the face of Christ.

Furthermore, if Christ is truly God by nature, have we not seen the glory of the Father in him? For even as we clearly hear God and the Father saying, 'My glory to another I will not give;' behold, He has given it to the Son.

Therefore, the Son is not another from Him, except insofar in subsistence and His own personal existence, so that the Father might not appear to have lied to the person of the Son by setting forth His own glory; and so that God is known to be in Him by nature and through Him.
For He is indeed a person, an icon, and a radiance of His subsistence; and the Son is revealed by the Father, and He Himself also reveals the Father to us within Himself.
In earthen vessels.

The term 'earthen vessels' refers to the common; for our tradition of the divine mysteries is not delivered to us in a pomp of words, but in a language accustomed to all, so that everyone might learn and understand.

What then, O Paul? For it was not possible for God, who makes all things wise, to make the holy apostles so extremely eloquent that they might easily, and even more than those being struck by the blow of words, amaze those who encounter them; yes, he says, for He Himself is the provider of wisdom.
But in earthen vessels—that is, in a small possession—He has locked up a treasure for us.
Through what reason? So that the excess of the power might be of God and not from ourselves.
In this way, He persuaded all to run toward the faith.
For if the word had been brilliant within them, it would have seemed that the faith of those called had not become an upright standing by His own power.
Since no one can be persuaded by bare words alone that he has become a partaker of God through the superabundance of this power.

We call ourselves pottery vessels, for we are bodies surrounded by perceptible things, thinking with such a mind; since we are still surrounded by the flesh, which hinders the vision of the truth, we possess knowledge concerning the Trinity, the excess of the greatness of this knowledge is not from us, but is made known to us by the power of God existing within us.
In all things they are afflicted, but not distressed (2 Cor 4:8)...
For they appear to have triumphed over death by their piety toward Him and by drawing from Him.
Yet even if they have had to suffer this, they nonetheless live, for they are destined to live with God.
And as the word of wisdom says, 'It seemed in the eyes of men' (Job 29:7)...
